sop-from-memo.output:
WATER HEATER SWAP

You will need
• Water shutoff at main (not just tank valve)
• Breaker for water heater circuit
• Garden hose from van
• Floor drain (or bucket)
• New flex lines (always)
• Expansion tank (if main has check valve — ASK OWNER if unsure)

Steps
1. Shut the water at the house main — do not rely on the tank valve alone.
2. Kill the breaker for the water heater.
3. Attach garden hose to tank drain and run it to floor drain.
4. Drain tank completely.
5. Disconnect old flex lines and remove old unit.
6. Set new unit in place.
7. Install new flex lines (use new ones every time, even if old ones look good).
8. Fill tank from house supply.
9. Bleed air at the closest faucet to the tank until water runs clear.
10. Restore power at breaker.
11. Wait 20 minutes, then check all connections and floor for leaks.
12. Photograph the new unit and connections for the file.

Done looks like
• No water running from tank or lines.
• No breaker tripped.
• Tank full and holding pressure.
• Air bled from system (no spitting at faucet).
• Photo in job file.

Common mistakes
• **Powering up before bleeding air** — you'll trap air in lines and overpressure. Check: water flows smoothly at test faucet, no gurgling.
• **Forgetting expansion tank when check valve is on main** — tank can't push water back, pressure builds, tank fails fast. Check: ASK OWNER if your job has a check valve on main line; if yes, confirm expansion tank is in place before power.
• **Checking leaks too soon (at 2 min instead of 20 min)** — cold flex lines settle and seal as they warm. Check: wait full 20 minutes after power, then inspect; small weeps at 5 min often stop by 20.

Maple & Sons Plumbing is hiring a service plumber to handle residential calls solo by month two. You'll work Monday to Friday, 7am to 4pm, plus one weekend in three on rotation. We provide the van. Pay is $28–34/hour based on skill and speed.

# The Quote Reader — MAPLE & SONS PLUMBING

**SYNTHETIC DATA** — sample calculation. Swap in your real quotes.

---

## 12-Month Cost Comparison
*(Normalized to owner's 3-year need: 18k miles/yr)*

| Vendor | Monthly | Setup | Mileage Overage | Maintenance | **12-Mo Total** | **36-Mo Total** |
|--------|---------|-------|-----------------|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **1** (36mo) | $890 | $1,200 | $660 (3k mi @ $0.22) | Included | $12,210 | $32,040 |
| **2** (48mo) | $740 | $0 | $2,160 (6k mi @ $0.30) | $1,140 ($95/mo) | $12,180 | $36,540 |
| **3** (24mo) | $960 | $500 | $0 | Included | $12,020 | $24,440 |

**Why the totals look close:** The cheap monthly (Vendor 2) bleeds miles and maintenance. Vendor 1's setup spreads across 36 months. Vendor 3 wins on 36-month cost but locks you in for 2 years only.

---

## Three Questions for Each Vendor

1. **If we go over 18k miles in a year, how is that billed? (Weekly? Monthly? At end of lease?)**  
   *Why: Vendor 2's $0.30/mile adds up fast. Vendor 1 is gentler but you need the ceiling in writing.*

2. **Can we exit early, and what does that cost?**  
   *Why: Vendor 3 offers month 12 exit at no penalty. Vendor 1 and 2 don't say. Business changes.*

3. **What's "maintenance" and what's extra? Tires, brakes, transmission work, roadside?**  
   *Why: Vendor 2 quotes $95/mo "extra" but doesn't define it. Get a list.*

---

## Recommendation

**Pick Vendor 3** — lowest 36-month cost ($24,440), maintenance + tires bundled, and you can walk at month 12 if the second crew doesn't pan out.

**Condition:** If you're **certain** you'll keep the van past 24 months *and* you trust mileage discipline, **Vendor 1** is safer (setup spreads, maintenance locked in, overage cheaper per mile). But Vendor 3's early exit is worth the ~$600 premium for a plumbing crew's risk.

**Avoid Vendor 2** unless you drop to 12k miles/yr or maintenance stays under $70/mo in writing.

---

**Status:** Draft. Review, ask the three questions, then you decide what to send or sign.
